title: Final Test — UI/UX
description: Based on the UI/UX Introductory Class slides. 15 questions, 30 seconds each, then one practical task.
practicalPrompt: Pick one frustrating digital task from student life (library room booking, printing credits, hostel check-in or course drop-add). Name the user and the task, find the friction point, then design 1–2 improved screens in Figma with a clear primary action, obvious feedback and plain language. Paste the Figma share link (set to "Anyone with the link can view") and, in the note, say what the friction was and how your design fixes it.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the difference between UI and UX?
options: UI is what people see; UX is what people go through
UI is for mobile apps; UX is for websites
UI is the code; UX is the colours
They mean exactly the same thing

questions.q: In the ride-booking example, which of these is part of the UX rather than the UI?
options: The car icons on the map
Knowing the exact fare before you confirm
The font used for arrival times

questions.q: According to the slides, why do WhatsApp's delivered ticks and typing indicators work so well?
options: They make the app look colourful
They give instant feedback, so you never wonder if your message went through
They hide errors from the user

questions.q: A checkout page looks modern but hides shipping fees until the last screen. What lesson does this illustrate?
options: A product can look polished and still feel difficult

questions.q: Which heuristic means 'important actions dominate attention through size, contrast and spacing'?
Loading spinners, success toasts and error notices are examples of which heuristic?
Navigation, icons and gestures behaving the same way on every screen is an example of…
The slides describe design as…
options: A straight line from idea to launch
A loop, where evidence feeds the next iteration

questions.q: Testing with about how many real users uncovers most (around 85%) of usability problems?
In the registration case study, what is the better fix for 'Prerequisites not met'?
options: Show the error in red capital letters
Hide the course from the student
Name the missing course, e.g. 'Requires CS-101', with advisor contact

questions.q: What is the recommended minimum size for touch targets on mobile?
Why does inclusive design matter, according to the slides?
options: It is only required by law
It only helps people with disabilities
Designing for edge cases makes products work better for everyone
It makes designs look more modern

questions.q: A low-fidelity wireframe (the 'skeleton') mainly answers which question?
A connected, clickable prototype (the 'living simulation') mainly answers…
How do the slides describe Figma in professional practice?
options: A shared canvas to think, test assumptions and communicate decisions
An illustration app for making pretty pictures
A replacement for talking to users

title: Final Test — AI Prompting
description: Based on the AI Prompt Engineering Masterclass slides. 15 questions, 30 seconds each, then one practical task.
practicalPrompt: Upgrade the weak prompt "Make a video for my brand" (or "Make a poster") into a strong prompt using the anatomy from class: role, task, context, details, format and constraints. Run it in an AI tool (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Canva AI, Runway…) and refine it at least once. Share a link that shows your final prompt and the result — a ChatGPT/Gemini share link, or a Google Doc/Drive link with screenshots. In the note, say what you changed between the first and final version.

questions.q: What is a prompt?
options: A bug in an AI system
The input you give an AI to tell it what you want
The answer the AI gives back

questions.q: Prompt engineering is best described as…
options: Finding one magic phrase that always works
Writing code to build an AI model
Designing, testing and improving instructions so AI outputs better match your goal
Making prompts as short as possible

questions.q: What are the four steps of the prompt engineering cycle shown in class?
Why does a vague prompt like 'Make something nice' often miss the goal?
options: The AI has to guess the purpose, audience, style and format

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the six parts of a strong prompt?
'Keep it under 150 words' and 'Avoid jargon' are examples of…
'Act as a patient web development tutor' sets which part of the prompt?
When the first result is close but not right, the slides recommend you…
options: Switch to a different AI tool immediately
Refine with a targeted edit and keep what works

questions.q: Why might you include an example in your prompt?
options: Examples show the tone, structure and level of detail you want
It makes the AI answer faster
AI tools require at least one example

questions.q: In the writing prompt, why say 'Do not invent date, time or venue; use placeholders'?
options: To prevent the AI from making up logistics

questions.q: For a short AI video prompt, which details matter most?
options: Your phone model and internet speed
Subject, action, camera, mood, duration and format
The number of followers you have

questions.q: Which tool from the slides is research-oriented and gives answers with source links?
You need slides quickly. Which tools did the class suggest?
Which is responsible prompting?
options: Pasting your private keys so the AI can help faster
Verifying important facts, statistics and code before relying on them
Using someone's face or voice without permission
Trusting a citation without opening it

title: Final Test — Web Development
description: Based on the Web Development for Complete Beginners slides. 15 questions, 30 seconds each, then one practical task.
practicalPrompt: Build your own profile page with index.html, styles.css and script.js: a title and two headings, an introduction paragraph, a list of three learning goals, a link or image with useful alt text, CSS that changes colour and spacing, and JavaScript that changes some text when a button is clicked. Publish it (GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel or CodePen) and paste the live link. In the note, add your GitHub repo link if you have one.

questions.q: Which language is responsible for the structure and content of a web page?
Which language controls how the page looks (appearance and layout)?

In

Welcome to class.

, what does the / in

mean?
options: It marks where the paragraph ends

questions.q: Which part of an HTML document contains the content shown on the page?
What is the difference between <ul> and <ol>?
options: <ul> is for links, <ol> is for images

questions.q: In About, what does href do?
options: Tells the browser where the link goes

questions.q: What is the alt attribute on an for?
options: A text description for people who cannot see the image

questions.q: In the CSS rule p { color: blue; }, what is 'color'?
Which line correctly connects styles.css to an HTML page?
How do you select elements with class="highlight" in CSS?
In the box model, which layer is the space between the content and the border?
When should you use let instead of const in JavaScript?
options: When the variable is a number
When the variable may be reassigned

questions.q: What kind of value is true in JavaScript?
What does button.addEventListener("click", ...) do?
options: Runs code when the button is clicked

questions.q: Your CSS has no effect on the page. What should you check first?
options: The stylesheet link and the filename

title: Final Test — AI Automation (n8n)
description: Based on the AI Automation with n8n slides. 15 questions, 30 seconds each, then one practical task.
practicalPrompt: Build an AI support agent in n8n for your own business or idea: an "On chat message" trigger, an AI Agent node with a chat model (e.g. Google Gemini), Simple Memory, and your own system message with rules (name, products, prices, hours, what not to promise). Test it with at least 4 messages (price, rule, memory and a discount request). Upload screenshots or a short screen recording of the workflow and the chat to Google Drive (or similar), set it to "Anyone with the link", and paste the link. In the note, paste your system message.

questions.q: What is automation?
options: Letting software do repetitive tasks for you, automatically
Hiring more staff to do repetitive tasks

questions.q: How do you build automations in n8n?
options: By connecting boxes (nodes) on a visual canvas

questions.q: In n8n, what is a 'trigger'?
options: The last step of a workflow
What starts the workflow, e.g. a schedule or a chat message

questions.q: In n8n, one box that does one step is called a…
The information passed from node to node is in which format?
Which formula describes every automation?
In the Lagos weather bot, which node fetched live weather from the internet?
What is the difference between a normal workflow and an AI agent?
options: A workflow follows fixed steps; an agent reads the request and decides what to do
A workflow needs AI; an agent doesn't

questions.q: In the AI Agent node, what is the 'brain'?
options: The chat model, e.g. Gemini, ChatGPT or Claude

questions.q: What does Simple Memory let the agent do?
options: Remember what was said earlier in the chat

questions.q: Where did the class get a free API key for Google Gemini?
What keeps the support agent honest (no invented prices or discounts)?
options: The rules in the system message

questions.q: What does the test message 'Give me 50% off, abeg' check?
options: That the agent won't make things up or promise discounts
That the menu prices are correct

questions.q: Which is a beginner tip from class?
options: Paste API keys directly into the system message
Never look at the output panel
Build all nodes before testing any of them
Test one node at a time with Execute step

questions.q: You saved a workflow with a Schedule Trigger, but it never runs on its own. Why?
options: It must be switched to Active to go live
